description: The File, Edit, View, Arrange and Extras menus of the draw.io editor: opening, saving, importing and exporting diagrams, editing shapes and their styles and data, controlling the canvas and panels, and the arrange, layout, insert and grouping commands. Shortcuts are given in their Windows/Linux form; substitute Cmd for Ctrl on macOS.

tools.name: File > New
tools.description: Creates a new diagram, offering the template picker with hundreds of categorised starter diagrams (flowchart, UML, ER, network, cloud, BPMN, mind map, mockup, floorplan) plus a blank diagram and a search box. On the desktop app it also chooses where the file is stored; in the browser it chooses the storage service.
tools.usage: File > New... (Ctrl+N in the desktop app opens a new window). Add `splash=0` to the URL to skip the storage/template splash screen.

parameters.name: Template search
parameters.description: Free-text search across the bundled template set.

parameters.name: Blank Diagram
parameters.description: Starts with an empty page using the default page size.

tools.example:
1. File > New.
2. Search "AWS" and pick a reference architecture template.
3. Name the file `architecture.drawio` and choose the target folder.

tools.name: File > Open, Open Recent and Open Library
tools.description: Opens an existing diagram from the device, from a connected storage service (Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, GitHub, GitLab) or from the recent-files list, and loads a shape library (.xml) into the left-hand panel. draw.io opens .drawio, .xml, .drawio.png, .drawio.svg, .vsdx and .mermaid files.
tools.usage: File > Open from > Device / Google Drive / OneDrive / Dropbox / GitHub / GitLab / URL; File > Open Recent; File > Open Library from > ...
tools.example:
1. File > Open from > GitHub.
2. Authorise and pick org/repo/branch and `docs/architecture.drawio`.
3. Every save now commits back to that branch.
tools.notes: A diagram can also be opened straight from a URL with the `#U` hash property, e.g. `app.diagrams.net/#Uhttps%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Fa.drawio`.

tools.name: File > Save, Save As and Autosave
tools.description: Writes the diagram back to its storage location, or to a new name and location. Autosave (Extras > Autosave, on by default in most hosts) saves a few seconds after each change, and the desktop app writes a .bkp backup next to the file before each save. The status line by the filename shows whether there are unsaved changes.
tools.usage: File > Save (Ctrl+S), File > Save As... (Ctrl+Shift+S). Autosave toggle: Extras > Autosave.
tools.example:
1. Make a change - the title bar shows "Unsaved changes. Click here to save."
2. Ctrl+S.
3. For a copy in a different format, File > Save As... and change the extension to `.drawio.svg`.
tools.notes: In embed mode there is no storage: Ctrl+S sends a `save` event to the host page instead.

tools.name: File > Import from
tools.description: Merges the contents of another file into the current diagram rather than opening it as a new document. Accepts draw.io XML, images (placed as image shapes), Visio .vsdx, Lucidchart, Gliffy and .csv data, plus Visio .vssx stencils as libraries.
tools.usage: File > Import from > Device / URL / Google Drive / OneDrive / Dropbox / GitHub / GitLab...
tools.example:
1. File > Import from > Device and choose `network.vsdx`.
2. The Visio pages are converted to draw.io pages and appended.
3. Fix any unmapped shapes by editing their style (Ctrl+E).

tools.name: File > Export as > PNG
tools.description: Renders the diagram to a raster PNG with control over zoom, border, background, resolution and cropping, and can embed the diagram source so the .png reopens as an editable .drawio.png. The usual format for pasting a diagram into a document, ticket or chat.
tools.usage: File > Export as > PNG...

parameters.name: Zoom / Border Width
parameters.description: Scale factor of the render and the margin in pixels around the content.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: Page, Diagram, Crop or Selection Only - what the exported bounds cover.

parameters.name: Transparent Background
parameters.description: Omits the white page background.

parameters.name: Include a copy of my diagram
parameters.description: Embeds the XML so the PNG can be re-opened and edited.

parameters.name: DPI
parameters.description: Sets the pixel density metadata and the render scale for print use.

tools.example:
File > Export as > PNG: Zoom 200%, Border 10, Size = Diagram, tick Transparent Background and "Include a copy of my diagram", Export.

CLI equivalent: `drawio -x -f png -s 2 -b 10 -t -e -o out.png in.drawio`

tools.name: File > Export as > SVG
tools.description: Produces a resolution-independent vector export, optionally with the diagram embedded (a .drawio.svg that stays editable), with links preserved, with the shapes' fonts embedded or converted to outlines, and with light/dark theme control. The best format for documentation sites and README files.
tools.usage: File > Export as > SVG...

parameters.name: Include a copy of my diagram
parameters.description: Stores the XML in the SVG's `content` attribute so it reopens in draw.io.

parameters.name: Embed Images / Embed Fonts
parameters.description: Inlines referenced images and web fonts so the SVG is self-contained.

parameters.name: Links
parameters.description: Automatic, Open in New Window or Open in Same Window for shape links.

parameters.name: Text Settings
parameters.description: SVG text (smaller, needs the font) or shape outlines (renders identically everywhere).

tools.example:
File > Export as > SVG, tick "Include a copy of my diagram" and Embed Fonts, save as `docs/flow.drawio.svg`, then reference it from Markdown.

CLI: `drawio -x -f svg -e --embed-svg-fonts true -o flow.drawio.svg flow.drawio`

tools.name: File > Export as > PDF
tools.description: Vector PDF export for printing and distribution, with page selection (current page, all pages, selection), crop-to-diagram, grid inclusion, fit-to-page and an option to embed the editable diagram. Multi-page diagrams become multi-page PDFs.
tools.usage: File > Export as > PDF...

parameters.name: Selection Only / Current Page / All Pages
parameters.description: What is exported.

parameters.name: Crop
parameters.description: Trims the PDF page to the diagram bounds instead of the page size.

parameters.name: Fit to Page / Zoom
parameters.description: Scales the diagram onto the paper size from Page Setup.

parameters.name: Include a copy of my diagram
parameters.description: Embeds the XML in the PDF so it can be re-imported.

tools.example:
File > Export as > PDF, All Pages, tick Crop, Export.

CLI: `drawio -x -f pdf -a --crop -o handbook.pdf handbook.drawio`

tools.name: File > Export as > XML, HTML, URL, VSDX and other formats
tools.description: The remaining export targets. XML writes the diagram source (compressed or not) for version control and scripting; HTML bundles a self-contained lightbox viewer; URL produces a very long link that carries the whole diagram in its hash; VSDX converts to Microsoft Visio; JPEG and WebP are additional raster options; and Advanced offers fine-grained control over the same renders.
tools.usage: File > Export as > XML... / HTML... / URL... / VSDX... / JPEG... / Advanced...

parameters.name: XML: Compressed
parameters.description: Untick to write plain, diffable XML.

parameters.name: HTML: Zoom, Layers, Tags, Lightbox, Link target
parameters.description: Which viewer controls the exported page shows.

parameters.name: URL
parameters.description: Encodes the diagram into a `#R...` hash - no server storage, but long links.

tools.example:
File > Export as > XML..., untick Compressed, save as `arch.drawio` so Git diffs are readable.

CLI: `drawio -x -f xml -u -o arch.drawio arch.drawio`

tools.name: File > Embed
tools.description:
Generates ready-made snippets for putting the diagram into another page: an HTML ``/`
` viewer snippet, an IFrame, an SVG or PNG data URI, a Markdown snippet, or the "Editable Diagram" HTML that includes the source. The starting point for embedding a live diagram in a wiki, blog or web app.
tools.usage: File > Embed > HTML... / IFrame... / SVG... / Image... / Markdown... / Notion... / Editable Diagram...

parameters.name: Lightbox / Edit / Layers / Tags
parameters.description: Which viewer features the generated snippet enables.

parameters.name: Width / Height
parameters.description: IFrame dimensions; Fit To Content is also offered.

tools.example: File > Embed > IFrame..., tick Lightbox and Layers, Copy, then paste the `<iframe>` into the documentation page.

tools.name: File > Publish > Link
tools.description: Creates a shareable viewer link to the diagram's current storage location with the viewer options baked into the URL - lightbox, zoom controls, layers, tags, link behaviour, edit button and a specific page. Anyone with access to the underlying file can open the read-only view.
tools.usage: File > Publish > Link...

parameters.name: Lightbox
parameters.description: Opens the diagram in the overlay viewer with zoom controls.

parameters.name: Edit
parameters.description: Adds an Edit button, optionally pointing at a custom URL.

parameters.name: Layers / Tags
parameters.description: Shows the layer and tag toggles in the viewer.

parameters.name: Current page only
parameters.description: Pins the link to one page of a multi-page diagram.

tools.example: File > Publish > Link, tick Lightbox + Layers, Create, then paste the link into a ticket.
tools.notes: The link only works for people who can already read the stored file - publishing does not change its permissions.

tools.name: File > Page Setup
tools.description: Sets the paper size (A4, Letter, custom), orientation, page background colour, background image and grid appearance for the current diagram. Page size drives page breaks on the canvas, PDF export and printing.
tools.usage: File > Page Setup..., or the Diagram tab of the Format panel when nothing is selected.

parameters.name: Paper Size
parameters.description: Preset sizes and orientation, or a custom width and height in points.

parameters.name: Background Color
parameters.description: Page fill used on screen and in exports (unless Transparent is chosen).

parameters.name: Background Image
parameters.description: An image placed behind the diagram, with its own position and size.

parameters.name: Grid Size / Color
parameters.description: Spacing and colour of the canvas grid.

tools.example: File > Page Setup: A3 Landscape, background #FFFFFF, grid size 10 - then File > Export as > PDF with Fit to Page.

tools.name: File > Properties
tools.description: Per-file settings stored inside the .drawio: the diagram's Math typesetting mode, the shadow default, whether the file is compressed, and the border/page settings that travel with the document. Useful for pinning a repository's diagrams to uncompressed XML.
tools.usage: File > Properties... (desktop and web).
tools.example:
1. File > Properties.
2. Untick Compressed so future saves write plain XML.
3. Save - the file is now readable in a pull request diff.

tools.name: File > Print
tools.description: Prints the diagram via the browser or OS print dialog, with fit-to-page or a fixed zoom, page selection, crop, and an option to print each page of a multi-page diagram. Preview shows how the diagram maps onto the paper size from Page Setup.
tools.usage: File > Print... (Ctrl+P).

parameters.name: Fit to / Zoom
parameters.description: Scale the diagram to one sheet, to an N x M sheet grid, or at a fixed percentage.

parameters.name: Page Scale
parameters.description: Multiplier applied on top of the paper size.

parameters.name: All Pages / Current Page / Selection
parameters.description: Scope of the print job.

parameters.name: Crop
parameters.description: Trims to the diagram bounds rather than the full page.

tools.example: Ctrl+P, Fit to 1 sheet across by 1 down, All Pages, Print.

tools.name: Edit > Undo and Redo
tools.description: Steps backwards and forwards through the edit history of the session. draw.io keeps a deep undo stack that covers geometry, style, data, page and layer changes, so most experiments are safely reversible.
tools.usage: Edit > Undo (Ctrl+Z), Edit > Redo (Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z).
tools.example: Apply Arrange > Layout > Organic, dislike the result, press Ctrl+Z to restore the previous positions.
tools.notes: Undo history is per session and is not stored in the file; use the storage service's revision history (File > Revision History) for older versions.

tools.name: Edit > Cut, Copy, Paste and Copy as Image
tools.description: Standard clipboard operations over the selected cells, plus Copy as Image, which puts a rendered bitmap on the clipboard for pasting into other applications, and Paste Here, which drops the clipboard contents at the mouse position rather than offset from the original.
tools.usage: Edit > Cut (Ctrl+X), Copy (Ctrl+C), Paste (Ctrl+V); right-click canvas > Paste Here; Edit > Copy as Image (when enabled).
tools.example:
1. Select a group of shapes and press Ctrl+C.
2. Switch to another page, right-click the canvas and choose Paste Here.
tools.notes: Pasting draw.io XML from the clipboard into the canvas recreates the shapes, which makes generated XML easy to test: copy the `<mxGraphModel>` fragment and press Ctrl+V.

tools.name: Edit > Duplicate
tools.description: Creates a copy of the selection offset slightly from the original, keeping style, data and internal connections between the duplicated shapes. Repeated duplication continues the same offset, which is a quick way to build a row of identical nodes.
tools.usage: Edit > Duplicate (Ctrl+D), or Ctrl+drag a shape, or hover a shape and click the directional arrows while holding Ctrl.
tools.example: Select a swimlane and press Ctrl+D three times to create four identical lanes, then rename each.

tools.name: Edit > Delete and Delete with connections
tools.description: Removes the selected cells. The plain delete leaves connected edges dangling; Delete with connections (Ctrl+Delete) also removes every edge attached to the deleted shapes, which keeps a flowchart tidy. Right-click also offers Delete Lane/Row when a container is selected.
tools.usage: Delete or Backspace; Edit > Delete with connections (Ctrl+Delete / Ctrl+Backspace).
tools.example: Select an obsolete process box and press Ctrl+Delete so its incoming and outgoing arrows vanish with it.

tools.name: Edit > Find/Replace
tools.description: Searches shape labels across the diagram and optionally replaces the matched text, with whole-word and regular-expression options and the ability to search all pages. Matching shapes are selected and scrolled into view one at a time.
tools.usage: Edit > Find/Replace (Ctrl+F).

parameters.name: Regular Expression
parameters.description: Treats the search term as a regex.

parameters.name: Match Case / Whole Words
parameters.description: Restrict what counts as a match.

parameters.name: Replace / Replace All
parameters.description: Substitutes the label text on matching shapes.

parameters.name: All Pages
parameters.description: Extends the search beyond the current page.

tools.example: Ctrl+F, search `^svc-` with Regular Expression ticked, Replace with `service-`, Replace All.

tools.name: Edit > Edit Style
tools.description: Opens the raw style string of the selected cell - the semicolon-separated key=value list that defines its shape, colours, geometry hints and behaviour - for direct editing. The fastest way to apply an exact style, to copy a style between shapes, or to set properties that have no UI control.
tools.usage: Edit > Edit Style... (Ctrl+E), or right-click > Edit Style.
tools.example:
Select a box, press Ctrl+E and replace the style with:
`rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;strokeWidth=2;shadow=1;`

For an edge:
`edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=0;html=1;endArrow=block;endFill=1;jumpStyle=arc;`
tools.notes: Right-click > Edit Style on several selected cells edits them together. Format panel > Edit Style does the same thing.

tools.name: Edit > Edit Data
tools.description: Attaches arbitrary key/value metadata to a shape or edge, stored by wrapping the cell in an `<object>` element in the XML. The data drives placeholders in labels and tooltips (`%propertyName%`), custom link behaviour, conditional styling via tags, and round-tripping with external systems.
tools.usage: Edit > Edit Data... (Ctrl+M), or right-click > Edit Data. Enable `placeholders=1` in the shape's style to substitute the values into its label.

parameters.name: Property name / value
parameters.description: Any number of custom attributes; `label`, `tooltip`, `link` and `placeholders` have special meaning.

parameters.name: Add Property
parameters.description: Adds another key; the rubbish-bin icon removes one.

tools.example:
1. Select a server shape, press Ctrl+M. 2. Add `hostname = web-01`, `env = prod`, `owner = platform`. 3. Press Ctrl+E and set the style to include `placeholders=1;` then set the label to `%hostname%
%env%`.

tools.name: Edit > Edit Geometry, Edit Tooltip, Edit Link and Edit Connection
tools.description: Precise per-cell editors reached from the right-click menu. Edit Geometry sets exact x, y, width and height (also available in the Format panel's Arrange tab); Edit Tooltip sets the hover text; Edit Link attaches a URL or a jump to another page; Edit Connection edits an edge's waypoints and endpoints.
tools.usage: Right-click a cell > Edit Geometry... / Edit Tooltip... / Edit Link... / Edit Connection... Geometry is also editable in Format panel > Arrange tab.
tools.example:
1. Right-click a shape > Edit Geometry and set x = 120, y = 80, width = 160, height = 60.
2. Right-click > Edit Link and choose "Page-2" so clicking it in the viewer jumps to that page.
tools.notes: Links to another page are stored as `data:page/id,<pageId>`, so they survive page renaming.

tools.name: Edit > Select All, Select Vertices, Select Edges and Select None
tools.description: Bulk selection commands. Select All picks every cell on the page, Select Vertices picks only shapes, Select Edges only connectors, and Select None clears the selection. Selecting only edges is the standard way to restyle every connector in a diagram at once.
tools.usage: Edit > Select All (Ctrl+A), Select Vertices (Ctrl+Shift+I), Select Edges (Ctrl+Shift+E), Select None (Ctrl+Shift+A).
tools.example:
1. Press Ctrl+Shift+E to select every connector.
2. Ctrl+E and set `edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=1;html=1;strokeWidth=2;` to restyle them all.

tools.name: Edit > Lock/Unlock
tools.description: Freezes the selected cells so they cannot be moved, resized, connected or deleted by accident - useful for background images, frames, floor-plan outlines and legends. Locking is also available per layer from the Layers dialog.
tools.usage: Edit > Lock/Unlock (Ctrl+L). Right-click > Edit > Lock/Unlock.
tools.example:
1. Place a floor-plan background image and press Ctrl+L.
2. Draw furniture on top without ever nudging the background.
3. Ctrl+L again with it selected to unlock.

tools.name: View panel toggles (Format Panel, Outline, Layers, Tags, Shapes)
tools.description: Shows or hides the editor's panels. The Format Panel is the right-hand style/text/arrange inspector, the Outline is a bird's-eye navigator, Layers manages the stack of layers on the page, Tags filters shapes by tag, and Shapes opens the library chooser for the left-hand panel.
tools.usage: View > Format Panel (Ctrl+Shift+P), Outline (Ctrl+Shift+O), Layers (Ctrl+Shift+L), Tags, Shapes...
tools.example:
1. Ctrl+Shift+L to open Layers, add a layer called "annotations".
2. Select the notes and right-click > Edit > Move to Layer > annotations.
3. Toggle the layer's eye icon to show or hide every note at once.

tools.name: View > Page View, Page Scale and Ruler
tools.description: Controls how the canvas represents paper. Page View draws page boundaries and breaks so the diagram can be composed for printing; turning it off gives an infinite canvas. Page Scale multiplies the printed size, and the Ruler adds measurement bars along the top and left edges with draggable guides.
tools.usage: View > Page View, View > Page Scale..., View > Ruler.
tools.example:
1. View > Page View off for whiteboard-style free layout.
2. Turn it back on and use View > Page Scale 75% so a wide diagram fits one sheet.
3. View > Ruler on, then drag from the ruler to place an alignment guide.

tools.name: View > Grid, Guides, Connection Arrows, Connection Points and Tooltips
tools.description: The snapping and hinting behaviours of the canvas. Grid draws and snaps to a configurable grid, Guides shows alignment guides while dragging, Connection Arrows are the blue directional arrows that create a connected copy of a shape, Connection Points are the green crosses used as fixed edge anchors, and Tooltips shows the hover text of shapes.
tools.usage: View > Grid (Ctrl+Shift+G), Guides, Connection Arrows (Alt+Shift+A), Connection Points (Alt+Shift+P), Tooltips.

parameters.name: Grid Size
parameters.description: Set in View > Grid Size or the Diagram tab of the Format panel; shapes snap to multiples of it.

parameters.name: Connection Arrows
parameters.description: Turn off when they get in the way of selecting small shapes.

tools.example:
1. Alt+Shift+P to show connection points.
2. Drag from a specific green cross so the edge is anchored to that exact point (it becomes `exitX`/`exitY` in the style).

tools.name: View > Scratchpad
tools.description: A persistent personal library pinned at the top of the shape panel. Dragging any shape, group or styled element into it stores that exact style for reuse across diagrams and sessions, and the scratchpad can be exported as an .xml library and shared with a team.
tools.usage: View > Scratchpad (or the Scratchpad section of the left panel). Use the Edit (pencil) button to rename, export or clear it.
tools.example:
1. Style a box exactly as your team standard requires.
2. Drag it into the Scratchpad - the style, not just the shape, is saved.
3. Click the pencil > Export to write `team-library.xml` and share it; colleagues load it with File > Open Library.

tools.name: View > Zoom In, Zoom Out, Reset View and Fit Page
tools.description: Canvas magnification commands. Reset View returns to 100% at the origin, Fit Page scales the current page to the window, Fit Page Width fits horizontally, and Custom Zoom sets an exact percentage. The zoom level is also shown and editable in the bottom-left corner of the editor.
tools.usage: View > Zoom In (Ctrl+=) / Zoom Out (Ctrl+-) / Reset View (Ctrl+H) / Fit Page (Ctrl+Shift+H) / Custom Zoom. Alt+scroll wheel zooms; Space+drag or right-drag pans; Shift+scroll scrolls horizontally.
tools.example: Press Ctrl+Shift+H to fit the whole diagram in the window, then Ctrl+H to snap back to 100%.
tools.notes: A few zoom and navigation shortcuts differ between the web app, the desktop app and the embedded editors - check Help > Keyboard Shortcuts in the build you are using.

tools.name: Arrange > To Front and To Back
tools.description: Changes the z-order of the selected cells within their parent, which decides what overlaps what. Bring to Front and Send to Back move to the extremes; Bring Forward and Send Backward step one position at a time.
tools.usage: Arrange > To Front (Ctrl+Shift+F), To Back (Ctrl+Shift+B); right-click > Edit > Bring Forward / Send Backward.
tools.example: Select the legend box that is hidden behind a container and press Ctrl+Shift+F.
tools.notes: Z-order is per parent: a child of a container can never be drawn behind a shape outside that container.

tools.name: Arrange > Direction (Flip, Rotate, Turn)
tools.description: Mirrors or rotates the selected shapes. Flip Horizontal and Flip Vertical mirror the geometry (and the shape's direction for directional stencils), Rotate Shape Only rotates the graphic inside its bounds, and Turn (Ctrl+R) rotates the shape 90 degrees clockwise, swapping width and height.
tools.usage: Arrange > Flip Horizontal / Flip Vertical; Edit > Turn / Rotate 90 degrees clockwise (Ctrl+R). The rotation handle appears at the top of a selected shape, and the Arrange tab of the Format panel has a numeric Angle field.
tools.example:
1. Select an arrow stencil and press Ctrl+R twice to point it the other way.
2. Or set Angle = 45 in the Format panel > Arrange tab for a precise rotation.

tools.name: Arrange > Layout
tools.description: Applies an automatic layout algorithm to the whole page or the selected container: Horizontal Flow and Vertical Flow (hierarchical, best for flowcharts and dependency graphs), Horizontal Tree, Vertical Tree and Radial Tree (for hierarchies with a single root), Organic (force-directed, for network graphs), Circle, and Org Chart. Vertical/Horizontal Flow is the one most people want for a flowchart that has grown messy.
tools.usage: Arrange > Layout > Horizontal Flow / Vertical Flow / Horizontal Tree / Vertical Tree / Radial Tree / Organic / Circle / Org Chart... Apply Layouts accepts a JSON layout specification.

parameters.name: Org Chart parameters
parameters.description: Type (linear, hanging, ...), parent-child spacing and sibling spacing.

parameters.name: Apply Layouts (JSON)
parameters.description: Arrange > Layout > Apply Layouts takes a JSON array, e.g. [{"layout":"mxHierarchicalLayout","config":{"orientation":"north","intraCellSpacing":40}}].

tools.example:
1. Select nothing (so the layout applies to the page).
2. Arrange > Layout > Vertical Flow.
3. If the result is too tight, Arrange > Layout > Apply Layouts and raise `intraCellSpacing`.

tools.name: Arrange > Insert (Text, Image, Link, Shape, Freehand, Table)
tools.description: Adds content that is not dragged from a shape library: a plain text label, an image (by URL, upload, or Google/OneDrive picker), a hyperlinked label, a basic rectangle/ellipse, a freehand drawing (Alt+Shift+P toggles the pen), a horizontal or vertical container, a table with a chosen number of rows and columns, and a page link.
tools.usage: Arrange > Insert > Text / Image... / Link... / Rectangle / Ellipse / Freehand / Table / Horizontal Container / Vertical Container, or the + toolbar button. Double-clicking empty canvas offers the shape picker.
tools.example:
1. Arrange > Insert > Image..., paste an image URL, tick "Fit image size".
2. Arrange > Insert > Table, choose 4 columns x 6 rows - a real container table is created whose rows and cells can be styled and linked.

tools.name: Arrange > Insert > Advanced (CSV, Mermaid, PlantUML, From Text, SQL, Template)
tools.description: Generates a whole diagram from text. CSV builds shapes and connections from tabular data with `#` directives; Mermaid and PlantUML convert their respective text syntaxes into native editable shapes; From Text builds a flowchart or a list from indented plain text; SQL builds an ER diagram from CREATE TABLE statements; Template inserts a bundled template into the current page.
tools.usage: Arrange > Insert > Advanced > CSV... / Mermaid... / PlantUML... / From Text... / SQL... / Template...
tools.example:
Arrange > Insert > Advanced > Mermaid, paste:
```
graph TD
  A[Client] --> B{Load balancer}
  B --> C[Web 1]
  B --> D[Web 2]
```
and click Insert - the result is ordinary draw.io shapes you can restyle.
tools.notes: PlantUML rendering uses an external service, so it is unavailable when the editor runs with `stealth=1` or fully offline.

tools.name: Arrange > Align
tools.description: Lines up two or more selected shapes by their left, centre, right, top, middle or bottom edges. Alignment uses the outermost selected shapes as the reference, so select the anchor shape last-position-wise and align the rest to it.
tools.usage: Arrange tab of the Format panel > Align buttons, or Arrange > Align > Left / Center / Right / Top / Middle / Bottom.
tools.example:
1. Rubber-band select a column of boxes.
2. Format panel > Arrange > Align Left, then Distribute Vertically.

tools.name: Arrange > Distribute
tools.description: Spreads three or more selected shapes so the gaps between them are equal, horizontally or vertically. Combined with Align it turns a hand-placed cluster into a clean grid in two clicks.
tools.usage: Format panel > Arrange tab > Distribute Horizontally / Distribute Vertically (also Arrange > Distribute).
tools.example: Select six icons in a row, click Align Middle, then Distribute Horizontally.

tools.name: Arrange > Navigation (Home, Enter Group, Exit Group, Expand/Collapse)
tools.description: Moves the selection and the view through a nested diagram. Home returns to the outermost level, Enter Group steps into the selected group or container so its children can be edited, Exit Group steps back out, and Expand/Collapse folds a container or group down to a summary box.
tools.usage: Arrange > Navigation > Home (Ctrl+Shift+Home) / Exit Group (Ctrl+Shift+Page Up) / Enter Group (Ctrl+Shift+Page Down); Collapse/Expand (Ctrl+Shift+X). Alt+click selects a child directly without entering the group.
tools.example:
1. Alt+click a shape inside a swimlane to select just that shape.
2. Ctrl+Shift+X on a container to collapse it and tidy a large diagram.

tools.name: Arrange > Group, Ungroup and Remove from Group
tools.description: Group combines the selected cells into a single movable unit; Ungroup dissolves it (and also converts a container back into plain shapes); Remove from Group lifts a child out of its parent container without deleting it. Grouping is also how a set of shapes becomes reusable via the Scratchpad.
tools.usage: Arrange > Group (Ctrl+G), Ungroup (Ctrl+Shift+U), Remove from Group (right-click > Edit > Remove from Group).
tools.example:
1. Select an icon plus its caption and press Ctrl+G.
2. Drag the group into the Scratchpad to reuse the pair as a single component.
tools.notes: A group is an mxCell with `group` style and `container` behaviour; a swimlane or a pool is a container with its own style and childLayout.

tools.name: Arrange > Clear Waypoints and Autosize
tools.description: Two clean-up commands. Clear Waypoints removes the manual bend points from the selected connectors so they reroute automatically, fixing edges that look tangled after shapes have moved. Autosize resizes a shape to fit its label exactly, which is the fix for text overflowing a box.
tools.usage: Right-click a connector > Clear Waypoints (also Arrange > Clear Waypoints); Arrange > Autosize (Ctrl+Shift+Y), or Format panel > Arrange tab > Autosize.
tools.example:
1. Ctrl+Shift+E to select every edge.
2. Right-click > Clear Waypoints so they all re-route cleanly after a layout change.
3. Select the oversized labels and press Ctrl+Shift+Y.

tools.name: Extras > Edit Diagram
tools.description: Opens the raw mxGraph XML of the current page in a text box for direct editing, and replaces the page with whatever XML you paste in. The most direct programmatic entry point in the GUI: generate XML elsewhere, paste it here, click OK and the diagram appears. Also the fastest way to inspect exactly what a shape's markup looks like.
tools.usage: Extras > Edit Diagram... (per page; switch pages first to edit another page's XML).
tools.example:
Extras > Edit Diagram, replace the contents with:
<mxGraphModel dx="800" dy="600" grid="1" gridSize="10">
  <root>
    <mxCell id="0"/><mxCell id="1" parent="0"/>
    <mxCell id="n1" value="API" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;" vertex="1" parent="1">
      <mxGeometry x="160" y="120" width="120" height="60" as="geometry"/>
    </mxCell>
  </root>
</mxGraphModel>
and click OK.
tools.notes: Invalid XML is rejected with an error and the existing page is left untouched, so it is safe to experiment.

tools.name: Extras > Plugins, Configuration, Theme, Language and Mathematical Typesetting
tools.description: The editor's own settings. Plugins loads JavaScript extensions (built-in ones such as `sql`, `tags`, `number`, `replay`, or a custom URL); Configuration stores the JSON configuration object described in the meta; Theme switches between Kennedy, Minimal, Atlas, Dark and Sketch; Language sets the UI locale; and Mathematical Typesetting enables MathJax so labels can contain LaTeX. Autosave and Compressed toggles live in the same menu.
tools.usage: Extras > Plugins... / Edit Diagram... / Configuration... / Theme / Language / Mathematical Typesetting / Autosave / Compressed. Configuration and Theme require a reload to take effect.

parameters.name: Plugins
parameters.description: Desktop: Extras > Plugins > Add. Web: the `p=` URL parameter for built-ins or `plugins=1` plus a custom URL.

parameters.name: Theme
parameters.description: Kennedy (classic), Minimal, Atlas, Dark, Sketch, Simple - also settable with `ui=` in the URL.

parameters.name: Mathematical Typesetting
parameters.description: Renders `$$...$$` and `\(...\)` LaTeX in labels through MathJax.

parameters.name: Compressed
parameters.description: Off writes plain XML in the saved file - recommended for version control.

tools.example:
1. Extras > Mathematical Typesetting (tick).
2. Label a shape `$$\frac{\lambda}{\mu} < 1$$` - it renders as typeset maths.
3. Extras > Configuration, paste a JSON object setting `defaultVertexStyle` and `defaultEdgeStyle`, then reload the editor.
